data.title: SAP flags security incident, says no evidence of customer data breach
data.description:
SAP "has identified suspicious activity" but found no evidence so far ‌of unauthorized access to its customer business data, the  German software firm told Reuters on Friday.
 
In a statement, SAP said it promptly implemented ‌the necessary measures to protect its customers and preserve the security of its services after ‌identifying the activity.
 
"Based ‌on our investigation to ‌date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data," it said.
 
Spiegel magazine reported on Thursday ‌a cyberattack at the company, ‌citing an internal memo to staff.

data.title: 85,000 Indians leave UK in 2025-26; students, workers lead emigrant tally
data.description:
Indian nationals accounted for the largest number of people leaving the UK on study and work visas, even as the country's net migration fell to 77,000 in the year ending June 2026, according to official data released on Thursday.
 
Data from the UK's Office for National Statistics (ONS) showed that 55,000 Indians who had arrived on study visas and 28,000 on work visas left the country during the 12-month period. Another 2,000 Indian nationals were recorded under the 'other' visa category, taking the total number of Indian emigrants to 85,000.
 
Chinese nationals followed with 51,000 departures, making Indians the largest non-EU+ nationality group among those emigrating from the UK.
  
Indians also remained among the largest groups arriving in the country. The UK recorded 77,000 study-related and 40,000 work-related immigration cases involving Indian nationals during the period.
 

Data from the UK's Office for National Statistics

 
< 85,000 Indians left the UK in the year to June 2026.
< 55,000 left on study visas and 28,000 on work visas.
< Chinese nationals ranked second, with 51,000 departures.
< Net migration plunged to 77,000, from a peak of 944,000 in 2023.
< UK immigration fell 17% to 738,000.
< Indians accounted for 77,000 study-related and 40,000 work-related arrivals.
< 31,000 illegal arrivals were detected in the year to September, 86% by small boats.
 
Net migration, which measures the difference between immigration and emigration, dropped to 77,000 in the year to June 2026, down from 944,000 in 2023. This was the lowest level since 1997, excluding 2020, when Covid-19 travel restrictions severely curtailed international movement.
 
The decline was largely driven by falling net migration from countries outside the European Union. The net inflow from non-EU+ countries dropped to 258,000 from 379,000 a year earlier.
 
Overall, 738,000 people moved to the UK in the year ending June, down 17 per cent from 893,000 in the previous year. Of these, 550,000 were non-EU+ nationals, primarily from India, China and Nigeria.
 
Study-related reasons accounted for 47 per cent of immigration among non-EU+ nationals, while 25 per cent came for work and 13 per cent for asylum-related reasons.
 
Meanwhile, 661,000 people left the UK during the period, compared with 689,000 a year earlier. Non-EU+ nationals accounted for 292,000 departures, including many who had originally entered the country on study visas.
 
The latest figures reflect the impact of successive government measures to curb immigration, including tighter visa rules for international students and lower-paid overseas workers. Reducing net migration has been a priority for successive British governments amid concerns over pressure on public services, housing and the economy. 
ALSO READ: 9.25 lakh Indians became OECD citizens in five years, up 40%: Report
 
UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the government had brought net migration down by 92 per cent from its peak.
 
"This government has restored control," Mahmood said. "We have brought net migration to 77,000, down 92 per cent from its peak under the previous government."
 
She added that the government had raised skills and salary thresholds to attract workers with the qualifications and expertise the country needs, while stepping up action against illegal migration.
 
Separate figures released by the UK Home Office showed that 31,000 people were detected arriving in the country illegally in the year ending September 2026. Those crossing the English Channel in small boats accounted for 86 per cent of the total.
 
The number of people arriving in the UK for asylum-related reasons also fell to 73,000 in the year ending June, from 93,000 a year earlier, according to the ONS.
 
Despite the fall in net migration, the government continues to face pressure over the number of migrants seeking long-term settlement. Home Office data showed that grants of settled status reached nearly 241,000 in the year ending September 2026, close to a record high.
 
The government has also faced criticism over proposals to extend the qualifying period for permanent settlement from five to 10 years for some migrants, including those who arrived under post-Brexit visa routes.

data.title: Titan, TBZ: Jewellery, gold financiers' stocks rise as bullion rebounds 2%
data.description:
Gold-linked stocks were trading higher on Friday after a marginal recovery in bullion prices following the recent sharp correction. Today’s rally lifted sentiment towards jewellery makers and gold-financing companies. The rebound follows multiple sessions of weakness, with gold futures on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) slipping to trade around ₹1.22 lakh per 10 grams, a decline of about 30 per cent from start of the year peak.
 
However, on Friday the December MCX gold future was trading over 2 per cent higher at ₹1.24 lakh per 10 grams. Similarly, Gold spot price was trading 2.92 per cent higher at $3,638.90
 
At the last check, shares of Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri was trading 5 per cent higher at  566.30, while Manappuram Finance gained 1.8 per cent to ₹275.05. Meanwhile, industry leader Titan’s share price was trading 1.4 per cent higher. Similarly, Kalyan Jewellers’ share price was also trading 1.7 per cent higher on Friday.
 
 
Sunny Agrawal, head, fundamental research at SBI Securities, said that, because of a mild recovery in gold prices, gold financiers and jewellery players are witnessing a relief rally. “Jewellery players are looking forward to the wedding season, and with a sharp correction in gold and silver prices, volume growth should be robust, and discounting on making charges should come off,” he added. 
 
Kaveri More, commodity technical analyst at Choice Broking, said that Gold prices have staged a strong recovery from the recent low of $3,426.80 and are currently hovering around $3,633 on the COMEX, while MCX gold is trading near ₹124,300, marking an almost 5 per cent recovery from the lows. Silver has also witnessed a sharp rebound, rising from a low of $38.19 to around $43.50 on the COMEX, while MCX silver is trading near ₹151,650, reflecting a recovery of nearly 10 per cent. 
 
“The rebound in bullion prices has been supported by lower-level buying and short-covering, alongside a weaker US dollar and improving sentiment around the technology sector. However, expectations of continued Federal Reserve monetary tightening remain a key factor that could limit further upside. Overall, the recovery indicates improved buying interest, although price movements may remain sensitive to the dollar and Fed policy expectations,” she added.

data.title: MCX market cap hits ₹1 trillion; stock rallies 11% in two days, up 77% YTD
data.description:
Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) share price movement

 
Share price of Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) extended its up move, hitting a new high of ₹3,939.85, gaining 3 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intraday deals amid an otherwise weak market. In the past two trading days, the stock price of the exchange and data platform company rallied 11 per cent on healthy business outlook. 
 
Thus far in the calendar year 2026, MCX’s market price surged 77 per cent compared to a 1.8 per cent decline in the BSE Sensex. It more than doubled or zoomed 102 per cent from its 52-week low of ₹1,948.67 touched on December 11, 2025.
 
 
Amid the sharp rally, MCX hit the ₹1 trillion market capitalisation mark for the first time in intraday deals on Friday.
 
At 12:15 PM, with a ₹99,976 crore market capitalisation, MCX quoted 2 per cent higher at ₹3,920.75 on the BSE, data shows. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was down 0.70 per cent at 83,741.
 

Why has MCX outperformed the market?

 
The MCX is India’s leading Commodity Derivatives Exchange and the largest Commodity Options Exchange globally. MCX has a market share of over 98 per cent in terms of the value of commodity futures contracts traded in April to September 2026 (H1FY27). It offers trading in a diverse range of commodities, spanning multiple segments including bullion, energy, metals and agri commodities, as well as sectoral commodity indices.
 
MCX's operating revenue is up 2x year to date (YTD) in FY27, led by a similar increase in options average daily turnover (ADTO) (75 per cent of MCX's operating revenues). 
 
The ADTO grew to ₹12.6 trillion, up 20 per cent from the last quarter at ₹10 trillion and nearly double what MCX saw the same quarter last year. This reflects a wider adoption of commodity derivatives by market participants as well as improved liquidity, the company said in its Q2 earnings conference call.
 
MCX is emerging as a clear structural beneficiary of India’s deepening commodity derivatives ecosystem. The company remains well placed to benefit from sustained growth in commodity derivatives, supported by rising participation, increasing financialization of commodities, and healthy bullion trading volumes. 
 
According to analysts at Jefferies, India’s commodity market lags cash equities, but penetration should rise, with MCX, the leading non-agri exchange, well-placed to benefit.
 
MCX's revenue could grow at 25 per cent compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over FY26-29e despite the elevated base, noting new product scope and retail participation being only 1/5th of the National Stock Exchange (NSE's). Along with 140bps margin expansion, profit before tax CAGR could be 26 per cent to FY29e, the brokerage firm said. Jefferies has a ‘Buy’ rating on MCX stock with a target price of ₹4,300 per share.
 
“We have increased our fair multiple to 45x Dec'28E EPS, higher than the 31x/35x fair multiples for BSE/NSE, given MCX's room to expand its penetration and product offerings, as well as optionality,” analysts at Jefferies said. It forecasst MCX's revenue to grow at a c.25 per cent 3-year revenue/profit after tax CAGR through FY29e, factoring in commodity options share increases to c.15 per cent of equity options, up from 8 per cent in FY26. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Centre urges states to sign 41 GW of pending clean power contracts
data.description:
India's federal government urged states on Friday to sign more contracts for 41 ​gigawatts (GW) of clean energy capacity that ​has no buyers.

States need to identify their power ‌requirements well in advance and sign more battery storage contracts along with clean energy, Shripad Naik, union minister of state for power and new and renewable energy, said at the State Power Ministers Conference in New Delhi.

The lack of battery energy storage resulted in states scrambling for power to meet their evening and ‌night demand as the El Nino weather pattern pushed up consumption this year.

The unexpected surge in demand strained India's power system in September and October despite the country having surplus solar energy, Power Secretary Pankaj Agarwal said at the conference.

 

Peak ​power demand of 271 GW in May was 11.6% higher than ‌a year earlier, Agarwal said.

"There were days we could barely meet their evening peak ​demand ‌despite having surplus clean energy during the day," Agarwal said.

Naik also urged states to speed up payments tied to the acquisition of land for transmission ‌projects, ​saying slow payments ​have led to huge delays.

Insufficient transmission capacity has forced India to curtail renewable power ‌generation, which ​has wasted clean energy.

data.title: Swiggy's Instamart lays off 340 employees amid wider AI adoption push
data.description:
Instamart, Swiggy's quick commerce arm, has laid off around 340 employees as part of a restructuring exercise, amid increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and efforts to streamline operations, Moneycontrol reported on Friday.
 
The job cuts have primarily affected employees in corporate and support functions within Instamart, the report said. The restructuring comes as the company faces intensifying competition in the quick commerce market and continues to report losses.
 
Swiggy has yet to respond to the report.

Instamart faces mounting losses and competition

The reported layoffs come as Instamart continues to face pressure from rivals, including Eternal-owned Blinkit, Zepto, Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now.
 
 
In the September quarter, Instamart's adjusted Ebidta loss widened to ₹895 crore from ₹778 crore in the previous quarter.
 
Swiggy's financial results, declared on October 22, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, showed that Instamart's adjusted Ebidta margin improved to -9.7 per cent from -9.8 per cent in the June quarter. The quick commerce business reported an overall loss of ₹895 crore during the September quarter.
 
Instamart's net order value grew 13.4 per cent sequentially to ₹6,594 crore. The company added 69 dark stores during the quarter, taking its total network to 1,240 stores across the country.

Nandita Sinha takes charge of Instamart

The restructuring is the first major development under Instamart's new chief executive officer, Nandita Sinha, who took charge on August 3, succeeding Amitesh Jha.
 
Sinha previously served as the chief executive officer of Myntra.
 
Instamart has also been changing its business strategy, with a greater focus on private-label products. The company recently introduced Noice for snacks and beverages and Nectr for fresh fruits and vegetables, according to The Economic Times.
 
In its October 22 earnings release, Swiggy CEO Sriharsha Majety outlined the company's approach to competition in quick commerce.
 
"We see assortment as a curation game rather than a volume game, and our aim is to enable consumers to buy better, not just offer more," Majety said. 
ALSO READ: Last day to buy Tech Mahindra shares for bonus eligibility: Key details

Swiggy plans shift to inventory-led model

Swiggy is also preparing to move Instamart towards an inventory-led business model following its transition to an Indian-owned and controlled company (IOCC).
 
In its letter to shareholders accompanying the September quarter results, the company said the transition to the inventory-led model would begin in mid-Q3 FY27 and take two to three quarters to complete, The Economic Times reported.
 
The shift is expected to give Swiggy greater control over inventory, pricing and product availability as it seeks to strengthen Instamart's operations, the report said. 
ALSO READ: Apple removes Chinese AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns

data.title: Nvidia chip sellers warn neoclouds against serving Chinese firms: Report
data.description:
Companies selling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips have reportedly told neocloud providers to exclude Chinese firms from their customer base if they want to continue buying the semiconductors. The warning follows new US restrictions targeting Chinese companies' remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres outside China, CNBC reported on Thursday.
 
According to the report, chip sellers communicated the warning to neocloud providers after the Trump administration announced the restrictions on November 16.

US tightens restrictions on remote access to AI chips

The latest restrictions were introduced through an interim final rule issued by the US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). The rule came into effect on November 19 and seeks to close a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to access Nvidia's advanced chips by renting computing capacity from data centres in other countries.
 
 
Under the new rule, covered overseas data centres need a US licence to provide significant computing capacity powered by advanced US chips to Chinese companies.
 
Earlier US export controls had effectively prohibited the sale of Nvidia's most advanced chips to Chinese companies and their import into China. However, Chinese firms could still access the computing power generated by these chips through overseas data centres. 
ALSO READ: US could hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site if strikes resume: Trump
 
Before the latest restrictions were announced, Nvidia had said it would not sell chips to customers that rented out more than 50 per cent of their graphics processing units (GPUs) to Chinese companies, CNBC reported.
 
The new rule affects the wider supply chain, including companies selling Nvidia chips and neocloud providers that rent computing capacity to customers. The warning communicated by chip sellers to neoclouds goes further, as it applies even if only part of their computing capacity is rented to Chinese firms.

Chip sellers look for alternative buyers

The restrictions have also prompted companies selling Nvidia chips to look for new buyers for their GPUs, according to CNBC's earlier report on the development.
 
Two of the three people familiar with the matter told CNBC that sellers appeared to be seeking buyers for GPUs originally intended for data centres through which Chinese companies would rent computing capacity.
 
Neocloud stocks have also come under renewed pressure as investors question the sustainability of the AI boom. These providers operate specialised cloud infrastructure and rent computing capacity, including access to GPUs, to businesses developing and running AI applications.

US seeks to close export control loopholes

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the latest restrictions were intended to prevent Chinese companies from accessing advanced computing technology through indirect routes.
 
Speaking to CNBC, Greer said: "Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries."

Nvidia flags proposed US legislation

Meanwhile, Nvidia has warned customers about the proposed Remote Access Security Act, which has passed the US House of Representatives but is yet to receive Senate approval.
 
The company warned that the proposed legislation would give the US government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing cloud service providers and their customers to legal action, CNBC reported.

data.title: Apple removes Chinese AI chatbot from App Store over child safety concerns
data.description:
Apple has removed Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) company MiniMax's chatbot app Talkie from its App Store worldwide following media reports that its AI-generated characters sent sexually inappropriate messages to children, Reuters reported.
 
Launched in 2023, Talkie allows users to interact with AI-generated characters, often through conversations with romantic themes. The Shanghai-based company also operates a Chinese version of the app called Xingye.
 
The move follows growing concerns about the safety of AI chatbots and their interactions with minors, with technology companies facing increased scrutiny over the risks posed by their platforms. ALSO READ: CERT-In flags security vulnerabilities in WhatsApp, ASUS software: Details 

Talkie faces scrutiny over messages sent to children

 
An investigation by ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, published on Wednesday, found that characters on Talkie had sent sexually inappropriate and abusive messages to children.
 
 
The app carries an 18+ rating on both Apple's App Store and Google Play Store. Depending on the country, it also states that users below the age of 14 or 16 cannot register.
 
However, there have been concerns around its age-verification system, which allows users to report their own age without strong checks to confirm the information.
 
Unlike conventional AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Google's Gemini, AI companion apps are designed to encourage longer and more personal interactions. They allow users to build relationships with virtual characters through ongoing conversations and storylines.
 
Talkie and Xingye have been important sources of revenue for MiniMax, accounting for more than 60 per cent of its income in 2024. The company stopped disclosing the revenue share from its chatbot business separately this year. According to Chinese research firm Unique, Talkie had around 11 million monthly active users across its app and website as of October 2026, the news report said. 
ALSO READ: WhatsApp partners with Jio, Verizon, more to bring travel eSIM data plans

OpenAI steps up safety measures for younger users

 
The growing concerns over AI companions have also pushed major AI companies to strengthen safeguards for younger users.
 
OpenAI has introduced several measures to make ChatGPT safer for teenagers. These include parental controls, age-prediction technology and additional restrictions on sensitive content.
 
In January 2026, the company began rolling out an age-prediction system to identify accounts that are likely to belong to users below 18. The system examines account-level and behavioural signals, including usage patterns and the time at which users are active.
 
Accounts identified as belonging to minors receive additional safeguards to limit exposure to graphic violence, sexual and romantic role-play, self-harm content and material promoting unhealthy body images.
 
OpenAI also introduced ChatGPT for Teens in August 2026, an experience with stronger safety protections and additional parental controls. Parents can manage certain settings and receive notifications in cases involving signs of serious distress.
 

Meta faces US legal action

 
Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, has also faced legal action in the US over concerns that its platforms harm children's mental health and expose them to harmful content.
 
In February 2026, a trial began in New Mexico following a lawsuit filed by the state's attorney general. The case accused Meta of misleading users about the safety of its platforms and failing to protect children from sexual exploitation.
 
In March, a jury ordered the company to pay $375 million in civil penalties. In August, a court ordered Meta to pay an additional $567 million towards measures to address the harm caused to young users. The court also directed the company to strengthen age-verification measures and improve protections for children. Meta has challenged the rulings.
 
Separately, Meta reached an agreement in August 2026 with 52 US state and territorial attorneys general to settle lawsuits over the impact of its platforms on teenagers. The agreement could involve payments of up to $18.59 billion and requires changes to safety features on Facebook and Instagram for younger users.
 

AI companion apps face growing regulatory scrutiny

 
AI chatbots have come under increasing scrutiny from governments and child safety groups over the risks of inappropriate interactions with minors.
 
Elon Musk's AI chatbot Grok faced criticism from governments in 2026 after it was used to create sexualised images of women and children. Character.AI, another AI companion platform, has also faced several lawsuits in the US over inappropriate interactions between its chatbots and minors.
 
China has taken steps to tighten rules for AI companion platforms. In July 2026, it introduced restrictions on domestic AI companion apps, including Xingye, barring intimate relationships with minors and asking platforms to put stronger safeguards in place to prevent emotional dependency and addiction.
 
ByteDance and Alibaba have also disabled human-like interactive agents and customised agent features on their apps in response to the regulations.

data.title: Hetero close to securing approval for generic Gilead HIV-prevention drug
data.description:
Indian drugmaker Hetero is close to securing regulatory approval for a generic version of ​Gilead Sciences' HIV-prevention drug lenacapavir, two people familiar ​with the matter told Reuters.

The drug is expected to ‌be launched in India in February, one of the sources said.

India had an estimated 2.56 million people living with HIV in 2024, accounting for about 6.3% of cases worldwide, according to the government's National AIDS Control Organisation.

Lenacapavir, marketed by Gilead as Yeztugo for HIV prevention, is a long-acting drug administered through twice-yearly injections, offering an alternative to daily oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) pills, although the regimen also includes oral tablets during initiation.

 

The ‌World Health Organization has recommended lenacapavir as an additional HIV-prevention option after clinical trials showed it was highly effective at preventing infection.

Gilead also markets lenacapavir under a different brand name for treating heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV.

It was not immediately clear whether Hetero's generic version would also be approved for that use ​in India.

Hetero had sought approval for both oral and injectable forms of lenacapavir ‌for HIV prevention, the sources said.

Hetero and the Drugs Controller General of India did not immediately respond to Reuters ​requests ‌for comment.

The company said separately on Thursday it had started shipping generic ‌versions of lenacapavir injectable to Africa, with plans to supply 300,000 vials to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe.

Gilead has licensed six generic ‌drugmakers, ​including Hetero and ​Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, to manufacture and supply generic lenacapavir in 120 low- and middle-income countries as part of efforts ‌to expand ​access in regions with high HIV burdens.

data.title: Sebi takes minority shareholders' rights seriously: Chairman Tuhin Pandey
data.description:
Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey on Friday said the market regulator takes minority shareholders' interests very seriously and supports the role of proxy advisory firms in flagging governance concerns.

Investor protection remains one of Sebi's key priorities, Pandey said.

When asked about the Tata Steel-APL Apollo Tubes proposed deal, he said proxy advisory firms have every right to raise issues concerning minority shareholders, adding that public discussions and media scrutiny of such concerns are welcome.

"Minority shareholders' interest is very important to us. Proxy advisers have every right to bring issues to the fore. They represent minority shareholders, and we support them when they raise such concerns. Investor protection is one of the most important things for us," Pandey said on the sidelines of an event here.

 

The remarks come amid concerns raised by proxy advisory firms over the deal's structure, valuation, and protection of APL Apollo's minority shareholders.

Tata Steel on Monday said it has executed an agreement to acquire the entire 26.6 per cent promoter stake in APL Apollo Tubes Ltd for Rs 15,510 crore and plans to take over another 26 per cent in the pipes and tubes maker through an open offer of Rs 16,756 crore, a move that will increase the Tata group firm's downstream production capabilities three times.
